viniyoga: Of this mantra, the Śrī Rāma Rakṣā Stotra: the seer is Budha Kauśika; the deity is Śrī Sītā with Rāmacandra; the metre is anuṣṭubh; its power is Sītā; its kīlaka (the pin that holds the mantra fast) is the glorious Hanumān; and it is applied in the recitation of the Rāma Rakṣā Stotra, for the pleasure of Śrī Rāmacandra.
dhyana: One should meditate on Rāmacandra: his arms reaching to his knees, holding arrow and bow, seated in the locked lotus posture, wearing a yellow garment, his eyes vying with the petals of a fresh lotus, gracious, his eyes meeting the lotus face of Sītā seated on his left lap, with the hue of a rain cloud, shining with many ornaments, and wearing a great coil of matted locks.
sh1: The story of the Lord of the Raghus spreads over a hundred crore verses, and every single syllable of it destroys the great sins of people.
sh2: Having meditated on Rāma, dark as a blue lotus, lotus-eyed, with Jānakī and Lakṣmaṇa beside him, adorned with a crown of matted locks,
sh3: And having meditated on him who holds sword, quiver, bow and arrows in his hands, the destroyer of the demons, who by his own play has appeared to protect the world, the unborn, all-pervading Lord —
sh4: The wise should recite the Rāma Rakṣā, which destroys sin and grants every desire. May Rāghava protect my head, and the son of Daśaratha my forehead.
sh5: May the son of Kausalyā protect my eyes, he who is dear to Viśvāmitra my ears; may the protector of the sacrifice protect my nose, and he who loves Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, my mouth.
sh6: May the treasury of learning protect my tongue, he whom Bharata reveres my throat; may the bearer of divine weapons protect my shoulders, and the breaker of Śiva's bow my arms.
sh7: May the lord of Sītā protect my hands, the conqueror of Paraśurāma, son of Jamadagni, my heart; may the destroyer of Khara protect the middle of my body, and the refuge of Jāmbavān my navel.
sh8: May the lord of Sugrīva protect my hips, the master of Hanumān my thigh-bones; may the best of the Raghus, destroyer of the demon clan, protect my thighs.
sh9: May the builder of the bridge protect my knees, the slayer of ten-faced Rāvaṇa my lower legs; may the giver of fortune to Vibhīṣaṇa protect my feet, and Rāma my whole body.
sh10: The virtuous person who recites this Rakṣā, which carries the strength of Rāma, becomes long-lived, happy, blessed with sons, victorious and humble.
sh11: Those who roam the netherworld, the earth and the sky, and those who go about in disguise, cannot even look upon one who is guarded by the names of Rāma.
sh12: Remembering the name Rāma, Rāmabhadra or Rāmacandra, a person stays unstained by sin, and obtains both the pleasures of this world and liberation.
sh13: Whoever holds in his throat this hymn, guarded by the name of Rāma, the one mantra that conquers the world, has all accomplishments in his hand.
sh14: Whoever remembers this armour of Rāma, called the Vajrapañjara (the adamantine cage), has his command unchallenged and wins victory and well-being everywhere.
sh15: Just as Śiva taught this Rāma Rakṣā in a dream, so Budha Kauśika, waking at dawn, wrote it down.
sh16: He who is a garden of wish-fulfilling trees, the end of every calamity, the delight of the three worlds: that glorious Rāma is our Lord.
sh17: The two are young, handsome, tender and mighty, with large eyes like white lotuses, clad in bark and the skin of the black antelope.
sh18: They live on fruits and roots; they are self-controlled, ascetic and celibate. These two are the sons of Daśaratha, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
sh19: Refuge of all beings, foremost of all archers, destroyers of the demon clan: may these two, the best of the Raghus, protect us.
sh20: Holding their strung bows, their hands on their arrows, bearing quivers of arrows that never run out, may Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa always walk ahead of me on the path to protect me.
sh21: Ready for battle, in armour, sword at his side, bearing bow and arrows, youthful, may Rāma, with Lakṣmaṇa, as he goes forth, protect our heart's desires and us.
sh22: Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, the valiant, he whom Lakṣmaṇa follows, the mighty; the descendant of Kakutstha, the Puruṣa, the Perfect One, the son of Kausalyā, the best of the Raghus;
sh23: He who is known through the Vedānta, the lord of sacrifice, the primeval Supreme Person, the beloved of Jānakī, the glorious, of immeasurable prowess —
sh24: My devotee who, full of faith, chants these names thus every day obtains merit greater than that of the aśvamedha sacrifice; of this there is no doubt.
sh25: Those who praise with divine names Rāma, dark as a blade of dūrvā grass, lotus-eyed, clad in yellow, are not bound to worldly existence.
sh26: Rāma, elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, best of the Raghus, lord of Sītā, the beautiful; the descendant of Kakutstha, ocean of compassion, treasury of virtues, dear to the brāhmaṇas, the righteous; king of kings, true to his word, son of Daśaratha, dark-hued, the very form of peace: I bow to him, the delight of the world, the ornament of the Raghu clan, Rāghava, the enemy of Rāvaṇa.
sh27: Salutations to Rāma, to Rāmabhadra, to Rāmacandra, to the Creator, to the Lord of the Raghus, to the Lord, to the husband of Sītā.
sh28: O Śrī Rāma, Rāma, joy of the Raghus, Rāma, Rāma; O Śrī Rāma, Rāma, Bharata's elder brother, Rāma, Rāma; O Śrī Rāma, Rāma, relentless in battle, Rāma, Rāma; O Śrī Rāma, Rāma, be my refuge, Rāma, Rāma.
sh29: I remember the feet of Śrī Rāmacandra with my mind; I praise the feet of Śrī Rāmacandra with my words; I bow to the feet of Śrī Rāmacandra with my head; I take refuge at the feet of Śrī Rāmacandra.
sh30: Rāma is my mother, Rāmacandra my father; Rāma is my master, Rāmacandra my friend; the compassionate Rāmacandra is my all; I know no other, none at all, I know none.
sh31: On his right is Lakṣmaṇa, on his left the daughter of Janaka, and before him Hanumān, son of the Wind: I bow to him, the joy of the Raghus.
sh32: The delight of the world, steadfast on the field of battle, lotus-eyed, lord of the line of Raghu, compassion in person and a mine of compassion: I take refuge in that Śrī Rāmacandra.
sh33: Swift as the mind, equal to the wind in speed, master of his senses, foremost among the wise, son of the Wind, chief of the monkey hosts: I take refuge in Hanumān, the messenger of Śrī Rāma.
sh34: Warbling sweetly the sweet syllables Rāma, Rāma, perched on the branch of poetry: I bow to Vālmīki, the cuckoo.
sh35: I bow again and again to Śrī Rāma, who takes away calamities, gives every kind of wealth, and is the delight of the world.
sh36: Roasting the seeds of worldly existence, winning happiness and riches, threatening the messengers of Yama: such is the roar of the name Rāma, Rāma.
sh37: Rāma, jewel among kings, is ever victorious; I worship Rāma, the lord of Lakṣmī; by Rāma the army of the demons was struck down; to that Rāma, salutations. There is no refuge higher than Rāma; I am the servant of Rāma; may my mind be ever absorbed in Rāma; O Rāma, deliver me.
sh38: Śiva says: Repeating Rāma, Rāma, Rāma, I delight in Rāma, who delights the mind. The name of Rāma is equal to the thousand names, O fair-faced Pārvatī.
iti: Thus ends the Śrī Rāma Rakṣā Stotra, composed by the sage Śrī Budha Kauśika. May it be an offering to Śrī Sītā and Rāmacandra.
